final_candidates.decision_summary: Introduces a charged glutamic acid into the hydrophobic core position V38, resulting in massive backbone/core incompatibility and efficient fold disruption.
Replaces conserved buried aromatic residue F40 with glutamic acid, severely disrupting core hydrophobic packing and destabilizing PsaE.
Mutates core aromatic residue F60 to glutamic acid, causing substantial structural incompatibility and knocking out subunit stability.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 candidate positions are well-established core destabilizing mutations with strong structural support.

history.rationale: W17 is a highly conserved core aromatic residue in PsaE; introducing a charged glutamate residue into this buried position will severely disrupt core hydrophobic packing and destabilize the fold.
Retaining strong candidate introducing a negative charge into a bulky hydrophobic position.
ProteinMPNN indicates relative structural compatibility (ΔlogP = -0.22), making it less likely to cause complete fold disruption.
F40 forms part of the hydrophobic core of the beta-barrel structure; substituting it with glutamate introduces an uncompensated negative charge that disrupts folding.
Retaining candidate replacing buried aromatic residue with charged glutamate.
High structural disruption predicted by ProteinMPNN (ΔlogP = -4.09), placing a charged residue into a hydrophobic core region.
F48 is a conserved core hydrophobic aromatic residue; a glutamate substitution causes massive charge and desolvation penalties within the protein interior.
Retaining candidate targeting core phenylalanine residue to disrupt stability.
Positive structure compatibility score (ΔlogP = +0.13) indicates high structural tolerance, counter to the knockout objective.
F60 is a buried phenylalanine residue; introducing a charged glutamate destroys hydrophobic core stability and promotes local unfolding.
Retaining candidate expected to disrupt local hydrophobic packing.
Substantial negative structural compatibility score (ΔlogP = -2.61) supports effective destabilization of PsaE.
Y16 resides within a conserved aromatic cluster essential for fold stability; mutating to glutamate disrupts local hydrophobic packing and electrostatic balance.
Retaining tyrosine to glutamate mutation aimed at destabilizing local structure.
Highly favorable ProteinMPNN score (ΔlogP = +0.88) suggests structural compatibility rather than required destabilization.
Y18 contributes to core aromatic interactions; substituting with a charged glutamate destabilizes the tertiary structure.
Retaining candidate targeting conserved aromatic residue in hydrophobic patch.
Strong structural incompatibility (ΔlogP = -2.59) and conserved aromatic position indicate reliable disruption upon glutamic acid insertion.
I37 is a core hydrophobic strand residue; replacing it with a charged, polar glutamate residue introduces severe desolvation penalty.
Retaining isoleucine to glutamate substitution intended to induce unfolding.
Positive ProteinMPNN score (ΔlogP = +0.12) contradicts destabilization goal as the mutation appears structurally tolerated.
L55 is a buried leucine in the core; introducing a negative charge at this location disrupts hydrophobic interactions and destabilizes the subunit fold.
Retaining leucine substitution to introduce severe desolvation penalty.
Near-neutral structure compatibility delta (ΔlogP = -0.10) suggests lower efficiency for complete protein destabilization.
V38 is a buried core beta-strand residue; glutamate substitution destabilizes central core packing.
Retaining valine to glutamate mutation targeting core hydrophobic packing.
ProteinMPNN shows severe structure incompatibility (ΔlogP = -5.20), indicating strong folding disruption at core position V38.
W17 is crucial for backbone conformation and core packing; mutating to proline disrupts secondary structure and causes backbone strain.
Retaining proline substitution to introduce backbone conformational strain.
Proline introduction causes backbone strain and severe structural incompatibility (ΔlogP = -2.44).
